chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from a man from the people of Kufa known as Abu Muhammad, from Amr ibn Shimmer, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The smile of a man in the face of his brother is a good deed, and removing the speck (of dust/annoyance) from him is a good deed, and nothing is more beloved to Allah than causing gladness to enter upon the believer.
ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved act of worship to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates mundane social etiquette to the rank of worship, highlighting that introducing joy into a believer's heart is the most beloved act to Allah. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *mu'amalat* (social dealings) as a pathway to spiritual perfection, where alleviating others' burdens is seen as a direct service to the Divine. The narration underscores the communal aspect of faith, linking personal piety with the emotional well-being of the community.
